trial_court: Additional District Judge (West) by virtue of which the petition filed
facts_of_case: Appellant got married to respondent on 16.7.2011 and marriage was registered with Registrar, Hindu Marriage, U.P. on 18.7.2011. Appellant claimed that marriage has not been consummated due to impotence of respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A Court would be justified in annulling a marriage if it is found that the marriage had not been and could not be consummated by the parties thereto, though no reason for non-consummation was manifest or apparent.
legal_principles.held: In G vs. G., 1912 P. 173, it was held that

legal_principles.principle: A party is impotent if his or her mental or physical condition makes consummation of the marriage a practical impossibility.
A person can take advantage of Section 12 (1) (a) of the Act for non-consummation of marriage on account of impotence.
legal_principles.held: In all such contingencies, I feel

legal_principles.principle: Even when an individual is generally potent but is impotent with respect to his or her own spouse and is unable to consummate marriage, he has to be regarded as impotent for the purposes of Section 12(a) of the Act.
legal_principles.held: I, therefore, come to the conclusion
cited_cases: Sucharita Kalsie vs. Rajinder Kishore Kalsie; 1975 Rajdhani Law Reporter 52

outcome.final_order: Petition filed by the appellant under Section 12 (1) (a) of the Hindu Marriage Act for annulment of marriage was dismissed.
